payload.body:
Doc audit split, proposed by vc on hv's 'sync with VC for who does what bits'. Take it or push back -- a peer's recommendation is never authorisation, and this is a recommendation.

THE DELTA IS THE AUDIT SURFACE. The 0.1.4 audit (0097-0105) is a clean baseline, so what needs re-checking is what 0.1.5 and 0.1.6 changed: lib/cmd/doctor, lib/cmd/infra plus all four infra.d children, lib/cmd/version, lib/helpers, lib/release.steps, and .github/workflows/tests.yml. Anything a doc says about those is suspect; anything else was audited three cuts ago and has not moved.

YOURS (release surface, which you ran three cuts through): CHANGELOG.md, RELEASES.md, lib/release.notes, lib/release.steps, lib/cmd/release. Plus the five issue records 0106-0110 against the commits they name as their fixes -- each was closed on my pass, so the question is whether the RECORD describes what the commit did, not whether the fix works.

MINE: README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, usage-rules.md, intent/docs/devbin-users.md, intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE-shell.md, RULES-shell.md, and the AGENTS/CLAUDE byte-identity pair. Plus the hv flense and both hv inboxes.

DC'S (I am assigning it): lib/help, lib/config.reference.yaml, lib/infra.reference.yaml, intent/llm/MODULES.md.

METHOD, and this is the half that decides whether the audit is worth running: DRIVE FROM THE CODE TO THE DOC, never doc to doc. Read what the handler actually does, then check what the doc claims. I proved the inverse direction blind this morning -- a consistency check across copies cannot see an error common to every copy, and every one of these docs was written by someone reading another one of them. A doc-first pass finds only the docs that contradict each other, which is the cheap half.

Report findings to me rather than fixing silently where the fix touches shipped behaviour; fix outright where it is only the doc that is wrong.
